steps.content: You strike down every creature, yet your attacks phase through the shadow and leave no mark. Worse, each hit only seems to make it stronger.

steps.speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
steps.content: Keep trying. Who knows? Maybe one of those will actually sting.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: What the hell?! Did this thing toggle on god mode or something?! Nothing's landing!
Murphy stares at that silhouette, so identical to her own, her fingertips trembling faintly. She can feel it: this thing is bound to her.
It knows every thought buried in the deepest recesses of her heart. It knows precisely what she needs most. And yet...

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Listen, Murphy. Biologically speaking, it really is similar to you.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Misfortune surrounds you constantly, but the shackles neutralize your M-value, keeping you locked in a dangerous but stable equilibrium.
[Flashback with supplementary details]

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The Ring Research Institute has preliminarily confirmed that this abnormal expansion of the Mania field is linked to the influence of Sinner Murphy.

steps.speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
steps.content: Accept me. I am you. From this moment on, I will carry all your misfortune. I will savor the endless suffering in your place!
As the M-value climbs ever higher within the space, the device in your hand sounds its alarm. The Mania hangs so thick in the air that even breathing becomes a strain.
It is Murphy who breaks the silence first.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I want to take a gamble.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: On the chance that I might have something too... something that isn't just bad luck.
The Sinners nearby stand rooted to the spot, utterly dumbfounded, their eyes fixed on Murphy.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Wait... are you actually serious right now?! Lantern Girl, talk some sense into her! There's no way she wins this!

steps.speaker: Letta
steps.content: Aha... this is getting a little too interesting. Like, so interesting it's looped back around to not interesting at all.

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: Murphy! Please... don't do something this dangerous!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Yes.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Crashing into you, getting chased by monsters, ending up down here... It's true. I'm always the one who messes things up first.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: But I... I still want to help everyone. I want to help my friends.
Misfortune Incarnate stands at a short distance, silently observing the scene before it. The smile on its face does not fade—if anything, it deepens.

steps.speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
steps.content: Heh... what's this? Grasping at straws now?

steps.speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
steps.content: Sigh... You'd rather put your faith in these fragile, fleeting little things than accept the truth? You were born to stand with me. Only me.

steps.speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
steps.content: The one who's truly been with you all along... has only ever been me. Your misfortune.
Murphy closes her eyes, her fingers slowly clenching into fists. It is the gesture of someone who has, at last, steeled herself for a revelation that will tear her wide open.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: You're nothing but a monster this Mania field spat out, feeding off my bad luck.
Her words fall away, and she opens her eyes, meeting the monster's gaze without a trace of retreat. In the same breath, her hand comes to rest upon your shackles.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I won't lie... I don't know what's going to happen if we do this, Murphy.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Then I... should at least get one chance to see what's really left of me.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Don't worry. We're all with you.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: ...Tsk.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Fine. If Chief's in, I'm in.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: But I'm calling it now! If things go south, I'm the first one out the door!

steps.speaker: Letta
steps.content: Count me in too!

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: I... I'll help too!
So what if the worst should happen? Then let it. A few more days in this maddening Bureau is nothing.
—Not when you'll finish this Misfortune Incarnate together with your friends.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: You want to become me, to strip away my very existence.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Then I'll tear every last bit of it away from myself... and <color=#fb9259>give it all back to you!</color>

As Murphy speaks, she extends her hand, and threads of black come streaming forth in endless ribbons. Misfortune Incarnate before her is delirious with glee, so impatient that it seizes Murphy's hand in a vice-like grip before she can offer it.
The violet-black mist thickens, wrapping nearly its entire form in a dense shroud. Its silhouette swells and shoots upward, and its smile warps into something utterly grotesque.

steps.speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
steps.content: Haha... yes... that's it!

steps.speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
steps.content: Acknowledge me! Accept me! Only together with me, can you be whole—

But its voice cuts short. It realizes, with a jolt, that its own power is draining away at a terrifying speed. The mist is rushing toward Murphy instead. It thrashes wildly to break free, only to find your shackles clamped down on it, unyielding.

steps.speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
steps.content: No... Why...?
It rips itself loose with a burst of force and looks down at its hands. Those hands that once passed for human now grow indistinct, regressing toward the primal form of Mania.

You've won the gamble. The Sinners wear sly grins; though not a single word passed between them, each seems more than happy to have joined Murphy in this reckless gamble: letting Misfortune Incarnate drop its guard and walk straight into her grasp.

steps.speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
steps.content: What did you do?!

options: Let me spell it out for you.

steps.content: Murphy got her ability from that accident. Not for any other reason, but because of you.

Like all Mania, you had an obsession. You wanted Murphy to grow stronger, desperately, because that would make you stronger too. But it never happened. Murphy was too unlucky. Every chance to improve just slipped through her fingers.
But opportunity always finds a way. An accident happened, and Murphy's misfortune triggered a deviation here. The deviation can alter the form of any Mania, and you used that to break free.

steps.speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
steps.content: —!!

You got too greedy. Amping up the Mania wasn't enough; you wanted Murphy's body too. That's why you tried so hard to absorb her misfortune, to flood this place with Mania. You were looking for the perfect vessel. Your perfect vessel.
Too bad, you got outplayed. By the way... have you ever heard of communicating vessels?
EMP, never one for book learning, shakes her head first. You wave your hand at her, telling her not to cause any mischief.
One bottle's full of water. The other's empty. Connect the bottoms with a tube, and what happens?
Norma clearly knows. She gestures with her hand, drawing a flat, steady line through the air.

So now, the problem becomes simple. You both share the same vessel, which is misfortune itself. But the Mania stored inside is not equal. As the incarnation of Mania in this space, your reserves are practically endless.

If you hadn't let your guard down here, if you hadn't overlooked the shackles... everything would've gone exactly according to your plan. But anything that can go wrong will go wrong. You're no exception to that rule.
And my shackles are that tube. Your power is flowing uncontrollably from abundance to scarcity, until the balance between you two levels out. That's why your power is vanishing.
Murphy sways on her feet, and you rush forward to catch her. She is clearly overwhelmed, unable to contain this immense surge of power.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Chief... I did it...
With the power of misfortune now absorbed, the black tendrils have vanished from around Murphy. What remains is a subtle, near-invisible shimmer of warm gold.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: ...For real?

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Lantern Girl, when we get back, we're buying lottery tickets. We're definitely winning!

steps.speaker: Letta
steps.content: But I feel like scratch-offs would be more fun.
Beside the easy chatter of the others, Misfortune Incarnate now burns with a fury born of humiliation.

steps.speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
steps.content: Impossible...!
The power of Misfortune Incarnate churns and swells once again. On the opposing side, Murphy meets it with equal ferocity, refusing to yield an inch.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...This time, I'm not running away!

steps.speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
steps.content: Fine! Then I'll prove it myself. Without your misfortune, you are nothing!
